draft.title: DNA structure
card: DNA is a double helix: two strands twisted around each other like a spiral ladder. Each strand is a chain of small units called nucleotides.
A nucleotide has three parts: a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar and a nitrogenous base. The sugar and phosphate parts form the backbone of each strand.
There are four bases: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C) and guanine (G). The two strands are joined by pairs of bases across the middle.
Bases pair in a fixed way: A with T, and C with G. Each pair is held together by hydrogen bonds, so the order of bases on one strand sets the order on the other.
draft.remember: Two nucleotide strands form a double helix, joined by hydrogen bonds between A and T, and C and G.

a.q: One strand of a DNA molecule reads A-T-G-C-C. What is the base sequence of the strand paired with it?
a.why: A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so each base on the first strand fixes its partner: T-A-C-G-G. Copying the same sequence is wrong because a base does not pair with itself. DNA has no uracil, so the last option is also wrong.
a.clue: Pair each base with its partner, one at a time.

b.q: A scientist tests a short length of double-stranded DNA and finds that 30% of its bases are adenine. What percentage of its bases are guanine?
b.why: Adenine pairs with thymine, so thymine is also 30%. That leaves 40% for cytosine and guanine, which pair with each other and are equal, so guanine is 20%. Choosing 30% wrongly treats guanine as equal to adenine.
b.clue: Each base has a fixed partner, so its amount matches that partner's amount.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: the complement of A-T-G-C-C is T-A-C-G-G, and 30% adenine leaves 20% guanine.
